reason: The gap is real. The round-18 W1 branch table (CONTEXT l.3037-3045) has rows only for 46 in P5/U4/N4/MASKED/NEG/ERR. Round 18 set a 46-read timer at 22:45Z that re-arms every 30 min until a hard edge at 00:00Z, but no row says what W1 does if 46 is still PENDING then. Without one, the 00:05Z choice would be made after the fact. The finding's runtime premise is weak, though. Dummy runtime does not predict hidden latency. exp70b's dummy took ~1,740 s (+15% vs K2's 1,512 s), yet its hidden L was (7.41, 7.58] h, the same as K2's (7.36, 7.54]. exp70e's dummy took 1,629 s and its L was (7.24, 7.42] h. Across 8 K2-family files the maximum L is 7.74 h (43/44). For 46 to still be PENDING at 23:45Z, L would have to exceed 9.13 h. I put that at about 5-10%, mostly from Kaggle-side delay. The fix is a single pre-score line and adds no mechanism. It reuses the existing rows (45 in P5/U4 -> exp76e, exp76a, exp76d; otherwise exp76a, exp76d with slot 3 held) and matches the table's conservative default. It touches none of R1-R10, the finals or byte-identity. It is cheap insurance, not a value lever.
fix: Append one dated line to CONTEXT now, before 45 is terminal if possible. The new row only extends existing rows, so it stays valid if 45 reads first. Quote the last poll.log header that shows 56611472 PENDING. The line: 'W1 PENDING ROW: if 46 (56611472) is neither COMPLETE nor ERROR at the last poll.log header before 23:50Z, W1 uses 45's code alone. 45 in {P5, U4} -> exp76e, exp76a, exp76d. 45 in {N4, MASKED, NEG, ERR} -> exp76a, exp76d, slot 3 held. exp76c, exp76g and exp73m move to W2 and are decided by 46's later read on the existing rows. The existing dummy fallback applies unchanged (exp76a -> exp72 -> exp75). A later 46 score never reopens W1.' When 45 reads, also log 45's ledger L next to K2's 7.36-7.54 h as a direct runtime check of the cap-6 change. Drop the '+24% dummy' argument; dummy runtime has not tracked hidden L (exp70b).
realistic_gain: No score gain by itself. It removes an undefined branch that has about a 5-10% chance of firing. That keeps W1 on time at 00:05Z and the choice pre-registered. It costs one CONTEXT line.
